provenance.data: NASA SPHEREx Level-2 spectral images, releases DR1 (spherex_dr1) and QR3 (spherex_qr3), read by HTTP byte ranges from the public copy at https://nasa-irsa-spherex.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/
provenance.finder: S3 header scan (IRSA SIA, TAP and IBE search returned HTTP 502)
provenance.measurement: forced photometry and a fitted position at JPL's predicted position (pxh.photometry.forced, each file's own ePSF), moved from the geocentre to SPHEREx with the header's spacecraft position; see docs/validation/pluto.md
provenance.outlier_flag: the pipeline's OUTLIER flag is cleared within 2.5 px of Pluto (it marks Pluto itself)

astrometry.selection: clean measurements with a fitted position at S/N >= 20

astrometry_snr10.selection: clean measurements with a fitted position at S/N >= 10

depth5_ab.method: 5 x 1.4826 x MAD of forced fluxes at up to 40 random positions in each stamp, at least 5 px from Pluto (the same estimator as Pluto's flux)

static_sky.method: forced flux at Pluto's position in other images of the same detector taken while Pluto was at least 40 arcsec away

spectrum.sunlight_shape: a 5772 K blackbody (a rough stand-in for sunlight), scaled to Pluto's median below 1 um; relative reflectance = Pluto / that curve

bands.name: Methane ice
bands.references: Cruikshank, Pilcher & Morrison 1976 found methane on Pluto by comparing its brightness at 1.55 and 1.73 um; Grundy, Schmitt & Quirico 2002 (lab spectrum of methane ice, 0.7-5 um)

bands.name: Methane ice
bands.references: Protopapa et al. 2017 (methane bands at 2.2 and 2.3 um in New Horizons spectra); Grundy, Schmitt & Quirico 2002

bands.name: Methane ice
bands.references: Grundy, Schmitt & Quirico 2002 (lab spectrum of methane ice, 0.7-5 um); Olkin et al. 2007 (Pluto's spectrum from 1.0 to 4.2 um)

difference_pngs.note: pixel values divided by each image's robust pixel noise; the single frame is shifted so Pluto sits at the centre, like the Pluto-aligned stack

shift_and_stack.method: S/N on difference images (each frame minus the per-pixel median of all the star-aligned frames): aperture radius 2 px, background annulus 4-7 px, noise = 1.4826 x MAD of up to 200 random apertures in the same image; inverse-variance weighted co-adds (pxh.imaging.coadd); the PNGs are the plain co-adds, before subtraction

difference_pngs.note: pixel values divided by each image's robust pixel noise; the single frame is shifted so Pluto sits at the centre, like the Pluto-aligned stack

shift_and_stack_faint.method: S/N on difference images (each frame minus the per-pixel median of all the star-aligned frames): aperture radius 2 px, background annulus 4-7 px, noise = 1.4826 x MAD of up to 200 random apertures in the same image; inverse-variance weighted co-adds (pxh.imaging.coadd); the PNGs are the plain co-adds, before subtraction

planet_x_geometry.assumptions: circular coplanar prograde orbits; Earth 1 au; within a visit, the track in every 7- or 14-day window seen 89.6 to 119.2 deg from the Sun (the Pluto images); between visits, two quadratures (solar elongation 90 deg) half a year apart

tombaugh.source: Lowell Observatory archives; Tombaugh 1946, ASP Leaflet 209

planet_nine.brown_holman_batygin_2024: with the ZTF, DES and Pan-STARRS searches, 78% of the predicted parameter space is ruled out; much of the rest is at V > 21

wise_0855.found_by: its motion in multi-epoch WISE astrometry
